message.content:
I don’t have real‑time clock access, so I can’t tell you the exact current time right now.  
If you need the precise time in New York City, you can check a reliable world‑clock website, use a smartphone’s clock app, or query a time‑service API (e.g., `http://worldtimeapi.org/api/timezone/America/New_York`).
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the current time in New York City?" We need to provide the current time. We don't have real-time data. But we can approximate using UTC offset. New York City is Eastern Time Zone. Current time depends on DST. We can compute approximate time based on UTC. But we don't know current UTC. We could say "I don't have real-time data" or we can approximate. The best approach: explain that I can't fetch real-time data. Provide instructions to get current time via API or system. But maybe we can use the function to get weather forecast? That doesn't give time. There's no function for time. So we should respond that I cannot provide real-time time. Alternatively, we can approximate by saying "As of my last update, it's X". But that's not accurate.

Thus answer: I don't have real-time capability. Suggest using an external source.
